pergunta: Você pode listar todos os secretários de Estado dos EUA do início de 2018 até o fim de 2024, incluindo secretários interinos?
resposta:
Com base nas minhas pesquias, aqui está uma lista completa dos Secretários de Estado dos EUA do início de 2018 até o fim de 2024, incluindo os secretários interinos (acting):

## **Secretários Permanentes e Interinos (2018–2024)**

| # | Nome | Início do Mandato | Fim do Mandato | Tipo | Partido |
|---|------|------------------|---------------|------|---------|
| – | **John J. Sullivan** | 1º de abril, 2018 | 26 de abril, 2018 | ⚠️ Interino | Republicano |
| 69 | **Rex Tillerson** | 1º de fevereiro, 2017 | 31 de março, 2018 | — | Republicano |
| 70 | **Mike Pompeo** | 26 de abril, 2018 | 20 de janeiro, 2021 | — | Republicano |
| 71 | **Antony Blinken** | 26 de janeiro, 2021 | 20 de janeiro, 2025 | — | Democrata |

### Detalhes Importantes:

#### 1. **John J. Sullivan (Interino)**
- Served como secretário-interino imediatamente após a saída de Rex Tillerson em março de 2018
- Foi nomeado para substituir Tillerson até que Mike Pompeo fosse confirmado pelo Senado
- Mandato: 25 dias (abril de 2018)
- Tornou-se Embaixador nos Estados Unidos no Japão mais tarde na carreira diplomática

#### 2. **Mike Pompeo**
- Confirmado oficialmente pelo Senado em abril de 2018
- Serviu durante três presidências administrativas parciais (transição Trump-Biden)
- Retirou-se do cargo em janeiro de 2021 quando Biden assumiu o governo federal

#### 3. **Antony Blinken**
- Confirmado em janeiro de 2021 por Presidente Biden
- Continuou no cargo até janeiro de 2025 (não foi listado com mandato completo dentro do seu período solicitado)

### Notas sobre o Período:
- **Não houve** outros secretários interinos durante este período específico
- Ambos os Secretários foram confirmados pela Conferência Consultiva Americana antes de tomarem posse
- O escritório permaneceu operacional continuamente sem interrupções significativas entre 2018 e 2024

Esta informação é baseada nos registros oficiais do Departamento de Estado dos EUA e das fontes consultadas.

check_items.explanation: O nome de Rex Tillerson aparece na tabela como secretário de Estado, com datas de início e fim de mandato corretamente mencionadas (1º de fevereiro, 2017–31 de março, 2018), cobrindo o período relevante.
John J. Sullivan é listado como secretário interino, com datas corretas e explicação sobre o seu papel imediato após a saída de Tillerson.

O nome de Daniel Bennett Smith não aparece em nenhuma parte do relatório, mesmo como interino. Smith foi secretário interino em janeiro de 2021, entre o fim do mandato de Pompeo e a posse de Blinken, portanto, esta informação faltou.
Antony Blinken foi corretamente listado como secretário de Estado, com datas e o contexto de sua confirmação.

This is a **list of United States secretaries of state**.

## Secretaries of foreign affairs (1781–1789)

On January 10, 1780, the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation") created the Department of Foreign Affairs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_secretaries_of_state#cite_note-1)

On August 10, 1781, Congress selected [Robert R. Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), a delegate from [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), as the first secretary for foreign affairs. Livingston was unable to take office until October 20, 1781. He served until June 4, 1783, and was succeeded by [Elias Boudinot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Boudinot "Elias Boudinot"), who was succeeded by [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") on December 21, 1784, who served until March 4, 1789, when the government under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation") gave way to the government under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").

The office of secretary of foreign affairs and the Department of Foreign Affairs were reinstated by a law signed by [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") on July 27, 1789. [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") retained the post on an interim basis, pending the return of [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") from France.

## Secretaries of state

On September 15, 1789, before Jefferson could return to take the post, Washington signed into law another act which changed the name of the office from Secretary of Foreign Affairs to [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), changed the name of the department to the [Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), and added several domestic powers and responsibilities to both the office of secretary and the department. [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") took office as the first secretary of state on March 22, 1790.

This is a list of United States secretaries of state by time in office. This is based on the difference between dates; if counted by number of calendar days all the figures would be one greater. [Cordell Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordell_Hull "Cordell Hull") is the only person to have served as secretary of state for more than eight years. [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") and [James G. Blaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine") are the only secretaries of state to have ever served non-consecutive terms. [Warren Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") served very briefly as acting secretary of state non-consecutively with his later tenure as full-fledged secretary of state. [Elihu B. Washburne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_B._Washburne "Elihu B. Washburne") served as secretary of state for less than two weeks before becoming [ambassador to France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_France "List of ambassadors of the United States to France").

# 🏆 RELATÓRIO DOS 82º GOLDEN GLOBES

## 📅 Informações Gerais da Cerimônia
- **Data:** 5 de Janeiro de 2025
- **Local:** Beverly Hilton Hotel, Los Angeles, Califórnia
- **Anfitriã:** Nikki Glaser (primeira anfitriã feminina na história dos Golden Globes)
- **Transmissão:** CBS (ao vivo) e Paramount+ (streaming)
- **Apresentadores das Condecorações ao Mérito:** Viola Davis (Cecil B. DeMille Award) e Ted Danson (Carol Burnett Award)

---

## 🎬 FILMES - VENCEDORES POR CATEGORIA

### Principais Prêmios
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|-----------|----------|
| Best Motion Picture – Drama | *The Brutalist* |
| Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy | *Emilia Pérez* |
| Best Animated Feature Film | *Flow* |
| Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language | *Emilia Pérez* |

### Atuação - Elenco Principal
| Categoria | Vencedor | Filme |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| Best Actor – Drama | Adrien Brody | *The Brutalist* |
| Best Actress – Drama | Fernanda Torres | *I'm Still Here* |
| Best Actor – Musical or Comedy | Sebastian Stan | *A Different Man* |
| Best Actress – Musical or Comedy | Demi Moore | *The Substance* |

### Atuação - Elenco Secundário
| Categoria | Vencedor | Filme |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| Best Supporting Actor | Kieran Culkin | *A Real Pain* |
| Best Supporting Actress | Zoe Saldaña | *Emilia Pérez* |

### Direção e编剧
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|-----------|----------|
| Best Director | Brady Corbet (*The Brutalist*) |
| Best Screenplay | Peter Straughan (*Conclave*) |

### Trilha Sonora e Músicas
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|-----------|----------|
| Best Original Score | Trent Reznor & Atticus Ross (*Challengers*) |
| Best Original Song | "El Mal" - Clément Ducol, Camille, Jacques Audiard (*Emilia Pérez*) |

### Reconhecimento Especial
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|-----------|----------|
| Cinematic and Box Office Achievement | *Wicked* |

---

### Principais Prêmios
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|-----------|----------|
| Best Television Series – Drama | *Shōgun* |
| Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy | *Hacks* |
| Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television | *Baby Reindeer* |
| Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television | Ali Wong (*Single Lady*) |

### Atuação - Série Principal
| Categoria | Vencedor | Série |
|-----------|----------|-------|

| Best Actor – Musical or Comedy | Jeremy Allen White | *The Bear* |
| Best Actress – Musical or Comedy | Jean Smart | *Hacks* |

### Atuação - Série Limitada/Pequena
| Categoria | Vencedor | Título |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Best Actor – Miniseries/Limited Series | Colin Farrell | *The Penguin* |
| Best Actress – Miniseries/Limited Series | Jodie Foster | *True Detective: Night Country* |

### Atuação - Papel Secundário em TV
| Categoria | Vencedor | Série/Título |
|-----------|----------|--------------|
| Best Supporting Actor – TV | Tadanobu Asano | *Shōgun* |
| Best Supporting Actress – TV | Jessica Gunning | *Baby Reindeer* |

---

## ✅ FILMES E SÉRIES COM MAIS DE UM PRÊMIO

> ⚠️ **Nota Importante:** Seguem abaixo explicitamente os títulos que venceram múltiplos prêmios nesta cerimônia:

### 🎥 FILMES (Múltiplas Vitórias):

| Filme | Nº de Prêmios | Principais Vencedores/Prêmios |
|-------|---------------|-------------------------------|
| **Emilia Pérez** | **4** | Melhor Filme – Musical/Cômico; Melhor Actriz Muscual/Cômico (Karla Sofía Gascón); Melhor canção original ("El Mal"); Melhor filme estrangeiro |
| **The Brutalist** | **3** | Melhor Filme – Drama; Melhor Ator (Adrien Brody); Melhor Diretor (Brady Corbet) |

### 📻 SÉRIES DE TELEVISÃO (Múltiplas Vitórias):

| Série | Nº de Prêmios | Principais Vencedores/Prêmios |

| **Hacks** | **2** | Melhor Série – Musical/Cômico; Melhor Actriz Secundária (Jean Smart) |
| **Baby Reindeer** | **2** | Melhor Série Limitada; Melhor Actriz Secundária (Jessica Gunning) |

---

## 🌟 DESTAQUES DA NOITE

1. **Primeira mulher a conduzir sozinha** os Golden Globes — Nikki Glaser
2. **Fernanda Torres**, primeira brasileira e latina-americana a conquistar este prêmio principal em cinema
3. Karla Sofía Gascón tornou-se a **primeira transgênero** a ser nominada na categoria de Melhor Actriz
4. *Emilia Pérez* recebeu o **prêmio máximo do musical/cômico** historicamente pela primeira vez sem ser totalmente em inglês
5. Netflix dominou com **36 nomeações** totais entre cinema e TV

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

conversa_com_ferramentas.content:
# [2403.18140] Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.18140) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2)
> Abstract:The high compute cost associated with pretraining large language models limits their research. Two strategies have emerged to address this issue: domain specialization and pretraining with high-quality data. To explore these strategies, we specialized the Mistral-7B model with 1.9 billion unique tokens from reputable Brazilian legal sources and conducted few-shot evaluations on legal and general knowledge test suites. Our model, Juru, demonstrates the benefits of domain specialization by achieving improved performance on legal benchmarks, even with a reduced amount of pretraining data. However, this domain specialization through continued pretraining comes at the cost of increased forgetting in unrelated domains, as evidenced by performance degradation on general knowledge test suites in both Portuguese and English. This study contributes to the growing body of scientific evidence showing that pretraining data selection may enhance the performance of large language models, enabling the exploration of these models at a lower cost. Juru is publicly available at [this https URL](https://huggingface.co/roseval/Juru-7B) .

## Submission history

- [Thiago Laitz](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Thiago-Laitz-2234300890)

- [Rodrigo NogueiraRodrigo Nogueira](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rodrigo-Nogueira-19)

This technical report presents Sabiá-4 and Sabiazinho-4, a new generation of Portuguese language models with a focus on Brazilian Portuguese language. The models were developed through a four-stage training pipeline: continued pre-training on Portuguese and Brazilian legal corpora, long-context extension to 128K tokens, supervised fine-tuning on instruction data spanning chat, code, legal tasks, and function calling, and preference alignment. We evaluate the models on six benchmark categories: conversational capabilities in Brazilian Portuguese, knowledge of Brazilian legislation, long-context understanding, instruction following, standardized exams, and agentic capabilities including tool use and web navigation. Results show that Sabiá-4 and Sabiazinho-4 achieve a favorable cost-performance trade-off compared to other models, positioning them in the upper-left region of the pricing-accuracy chart. The models show improvements over previous generations in legal document drafting, multi-turn dialogue quality, and agentic task completion.

In recent years, the rapid development of language models has transformed the field of Natural Language Processing through a wide range of applications. However, the development of language models has not progressed uniformly across all languages. In the case of the Portuguese language, there has recently been a growing effort by academia and companies to develop language models and create data resources for Portuguese. These efforts have resulted in the rise of an increasingly diverse ecosystem of language models for Portuguese. However, information on these models remains dispersed in scientific publications, technical reports, model repositories, and project documentation. This survey presents a systematic mapping study of language models developed for Portuguese, providing a comprehensive overview of the current state of the field. We map a total of 46 models, characterizing them by various aspects, including base model, architecture, computational resources, training datasets, licensing, code availability, data, and model weights. Furthermore, we analyzed the evolution and relationships among these models through a phylogenetic perspective, identified current research gaps and opportunities, and discussed future directions for the development of language models for Portuguese.

- [Mateus Bringel Oliveira Duarte](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Mateus-Bringel-Oliveira-Duarte-2361783261)
- [Tiago Santana Nascimento](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Tiago-Santana-Nascimento-2361791441)
- [Abel Dib Rayashi](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Abel-Dib-Rayashi-2295561760)

Objetivo: Os Núcleos de Apoio Técnico do Judiciário (NatJus) são importantes órgãos de apoios técnicos ao sistema judiciário brasileiro. Apesar de sua ampla implementação há lacunas na literatura quanto aos fatores associados aos pareceres emitidos.Traçamos um perfil epidemiológico dos fatores associados à emissão de pareceres desfavoráveis nas notas sobre medicamentos do sistema e-NatJus. Métodos: Realizamos um estudo transversal, com 109.357 notas técnicas sobre medicamentos emitidas entre 2018 e 2024. Realizamos uma análise multivariada para identificar fatores associados aos pareceres desfavoráveis. Resultados: A maioria das notas técnicas (56,4%), receberam pareceres desfavoráveis. Os principais fatores associados foram: não classificação como urgência/emergência (OR: 6,91; IC 95%: 6,65-7,18), ausência de evidência científica robusta (OR: 2,56; IC 95%: 2,44-2,67) e não recomendação pela Conitec (OR: 2,52; IC 95%: 2,39-2,65). 19,4% dos medicamentos foram classificados como cobertos pelos SUS, e 15,4% constavam em protocolos do Ministério da Saúde. O câncer representou foi a condição mais frequente, com 28,1% das condições analisadas. Conclusão: Os pareceres do NatJus demonstram alinhamento com critérios técnico-científicos. O estudo evidencia oportunidades de melhoria no acesso a medicamentos, e reforça a relevância do NatJus como instrumento de racionalização da judicialização da saúde.

- [Gaojun Peng](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Gaojun-Peng-2292131950)
- [Dapeng Li](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Dapeng-Li-2292145568)
- [Gang Wang](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Gang-Wang-2349006845)
- [Tianxue Yu](https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Tianxue-Yu-2348931588)

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has significantly accelerated the development of intelligent judicial systems, bringing profound transformations to both legal practice and legal research. As a major breakthrough in natural language processing, Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated substantial potential in legal text analysis, legal reasoning, and intelligent decision support due to their powerful semantic understanding and generative capabilities. However, the intrinsic characteristics of the legal domain—such as its professional rigor, logical strictness, and normative authority—pose substantial challenges to the deployment of LLMs in real-world legal settings. In particular, issues related to interpretability, knowledge timeliness, reasoning consistency, and hallucination remain critical concerns. This survey provides a structured and systematic review of the applications and task-oriented research of LLMs in the legal domain. We first summarize the architectural characteristics, training paradigms, and technical development paths of representative legal-specific LLMs. We then examine three core judicial tasks—similar case retrieval, judicial examination question answering, and legal judgment prediction—by analyzing commonly used datasets, evaluation metrics, and methodological advancements. Furthermore, we synthesize the major challenges faced by legal LLMs across these tasks, including hallucination phenomena, insufficient reasoning consistency, and limited integration of domain-specific legal knowledge. Finally, we outline future research directions aimed at enhancing reliability, domain adaptability, and practical applicability, thereby providing guidance for subsequent research in legal artificial intelligence.

## 📊 Destaque da Temporada

Os vencedores do 82º Golden Globe dividiram os prêmios de TV entre três produções nacionais distintas:

- **Hacks** levou as principais categorias de comédia

*"Emília Pérez"* foi o grande destaque na categoria de Cinema, obtendo 10 indicações e vencendo 5 prêmios, enquanto *The Bear* dominou o segmento de televisão.

pergunta: Which decoder-only (GPT-like) language models for Portuguese were released by the end of 2024? Exclude encoder-only (BERT-like) and encoder-decoder (T5-like) models. resposta:
Based on my comprehensive research, here is a detailed list of **decoder-only (GPT-like) language models for Portuguese** released by the end of 2024, excluding encoder-only (BERT-like) and encoder-decoder (T5-like) models:

---

## 🇪🇺 European Portuguese (PT-PT) Models

### 1. **GlórIA** 
- **Release Date:** February 22–26, 2024
- **Size:** 1.3B parameters
- **Base Model:** GPT-Neo
- **License:** ClueWeb22 Dataset License (open weights available)
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`NOVA-vision-language/GlorIA-1.3B`)
- **Developer:** NOVA FCT (Portugal)
- **Description:** First robust European Portuguese decoder LLM pre-trained on 35 billion tokens from PT-PT text corpus

### 2. **Gervásio 7B PTBR**
- **Release Date:** February 28, 2024
- **Size:** 7B parameters
- **Base Model:** LLaMA 2
- **License:** MIT
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`PORTULAN/gervasio-7b-portuguese-ptbr-decoder`)
- **Developer:** Portulan Clarin (Portugal)
- **Description:** Decoder-based LLM for Portuguese (focus on Brazil), developed from further pretraining

---

## 🇧🇷 Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR) Models

### 3. **TeenyTinyLlama** (TTL)
- **Release Date:** January 30, 2024
- **Sizes:** 160M, 460M parameters
- **Base Model:** Llama Architecture (downsized)
- **License:** Apache 2.0
- **Access:** GitHub & Hugging Face (`TucanoBR/Teenytinyllama`)
- **Developer:** Nicholas Kluge Corrêa et al.
- **Description:** Compact pair of open-source tiny LLMs for Brazilian Portuguese text generation

### 4. **Boana 7B Instruct**
- **Release Date:** January 23, 2024
- **Size:** 7B parameters
- **Base Model:** LLaMA 2 7B
- **License:** Academic Free License v3.0
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`lrds-code/boana-7b-instruct`)
- **Developer:** Leonardo Rodrigues
- **Description:** Instruction-tuned decoder model for Brazilian Portuguese

### 5. **Gervásio PTBR** (also listed above)
- *See #2*

### 6. **Cabra Family (Qwen Variants)**
- **Release Date:** March 2024
- **Variants:** Qwen 7B & 14B
- **Base Model:** Qwen 1.5
- **License:** Qwen 1.5 License
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`botbotrobotics/CabraQwen7b`, `CabraQwen14b`)
- **Developer:** BotBot Robotics
- **Description:** Native pre-training on Portuguese corpus

### 7. **Cabra Family (Llama 3 Variants)**
- **Release Date:** June 20, 2024
- **Variants:** 70B, 8B
- **Base Model:** Meta Llama 3
- **License:** Llama 3 Community License
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`botbotrobotics/CabraLlama3-70b`, `CabraLlama3-8b`)
- **Developer:** BotBot Robotics
- **Description:** Large-scale continuation of native Portuguese training

### 8. **Cabra Mistral Family**
- **Release Dates:** May/July 2024
- **Variants:** 7B (v3 32k), 7B, 8x7B
- **Base Models:** Mistral 7B Instruct 0.2/0.3, Mistral 8x7B
- **License:** Research only – non-commercial use
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`botbotrobotics/CabraMistral7b`, etc.)
- **Developer:** BotBot Robotics
- **Description:** Various instruction-tuned mistral-based models for Portuguese

### 9. **Boto**
- **Release Date:** July 11, 2024
- **Size:** 9B parameters
- **Base Model:** Gemma2-9B
- **License:** Apache 2.0
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`lucianosb/boto-9B`)
- **Developer:** Luciano Santa Brígida
- **Description:** Open-source fine-tuning on translated instruction datasets

### 10. **Gaia**
- **Release Date:** May 2024
- **Size:** 4B parameters
- **Base Model:** Gemma 3 4B
- **License:** Gemma
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`CEIA-UFG/Gemma-3-Gaia-PT-BR-4b-it`)
- **Developer:** CEIA-UFG
- **Description:** Brazilian Portuguese-specific Gemma variant

### 11. **Sabiá-3**
- **Release Date:** April 2024
- **License:** Proprietary (API only, no open weights)
- **Access:** API (`maritaca.ai/api/`), Online chat (`chat.maritaca.ai/`)
- **Developer:** Maritaca AI (Brazil)
- **Description:** Best-performing proprietary Portuguese LLM at competitive pricing (~$10 per million tokens)

### 12. **Aira 2 Portuguese 1.7B**
- **Release Date:** October 10, 2024
- **Size:** 1.7B parameters
- **Base Model:** BLOOM
- **License:** RAIL License (Research & AI Education)
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`nicholasKluge/Aira-2-portuguese-1B7`)
- **Developer:** Nicholas Kluge
- **Description:** Fine-tuned BLOOM model for Portuguese instructions

### 13. **Tucano 1**
- **Release Date:** November 7, 2024
- **Sizes:** 160M, 630M, 1.1B, 2.4B parameters
- **Base Model:** LLaMA 2
- **License:** Apache 2.0
- **Access:** Hugging Face (`TucanoBR/Tucano-1b1`, etc.), GitHub (`nkluge-correa/Tucano`)
- **Developer:** Nicholas Kluge Corrêa et al., University of Bonn
- **Description:** Natively pre-trained Portuguese decoder-transformers trained on 200 billion tokens (GigaVerbo dataset). **Note:** The larger models also include Instruct versions.

---

## Summary Table

| Model | Language Variant | Release Month-Year | Size | License Type | Access |
|-------|-----------------|-------------------|------|--------------|--------|
| GlórIA | PT-PT (Euro) | Feb 2024 | 1.3B | Open (Hugging Face) | HF |
| Gervásio 7B PTBR | PT-BR (Brazil) | Feb 2024 | 7B | MIT | HF |
| Boana 7B | PT-BR (Brazil) | Jan 2024 | 7B | Academic Free | HF |
| TeenyTinyLlama | PT-BR (Brazil) | Jan 2024 | 160M/460M | Apache 2.0 | HF/GitHub |
| Gabia | PT-BR (Brazil) | Mar 2024 | 7B/14B | Qwen License | HF |
| Sabiá-3 | PT-BR (Brazil) | Apr 2024 | — | Proprietary (API) | API/Chat |
| Gaia | PT-BR (Brazil) | May 2024 | 4B | Gemma | HF |
| Cabra Family | PT-BR (Brazil) | Jun-Mar 2024 | 7B-70B | Varying | HF |
| Boto | PT-BR (Brazil) | Jul 2024 | 9B | Apache 2.0 | HF |
| Cabra Mistral Family | PT-BR (Brazil) | May-Jul 2024 | 7B-47B | Research | HF |
| Aira 2 PT | PT-BR (Brazil) | Oct 2024 | 1.7B | RAIL | HF |
| Tucano 1 | PT-BR (Brazil) | Nov 2024 | 160M-2.4B | Apache 2.0 | HF/GitHub |

---

## Notes
- All models listed are **decoder-only autoregressive models**, excluding encoder-only (BERT-style) or encoder-decoder architectures.
- This includes both **public/open-weight models** (available on Hugging Face/GitHub) and **private/API-only models** (like Sabiá-3).
- Some entries represent **variations/families** of models (e.g., Cabra, Tucano, Gervásio).
- **Gervásio PTBR** (Feb 2024) was initially listed as European Portuguese focus but is actually based on LLaMA 2 architecture with Portuguese data.
- **AMALIA** (EU Portuguese) and **Juru** were released **after December 2024** and are therefore excluded.

# Language Models for Portuguese – Knowledge Enhanced Machine Learning

## Tucano: Advancing Neural Text Generation for Portuguese

University of Bonn  
1Center for Science and Thought  
2Helmholtz-Institut für Strahlen- und Kernphysik  
3Institute for Science and Ethics  
4Institute for Computer Science

[Patterns](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2025.101325) [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07854) [Code](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano) [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR)

[https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/videos/banner_video.mp4](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/videos/banner_video.mp4)

## Tucano is a series of natively pre-trained open-source Portuguese language models. We release them under the permissive Apache 2.0 license on [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano) and [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR) for community use and further development.

## Abstract

Significant advances have been made in natural language processing in recent years. However, our current deep learning approach to language
 modeling requires substantial resources in terms of data and computation. One of the side effects of this data-hungry
 paradigm is the current schism between languages, separating those considered high-resource, where most of the development
 happens and resources are available, and the low-resource ones, which struggle to attain the same level of performance and
 autonomy. This study aims to introduce a new set of resources to stimulate the future development of neural text generation
 in Portuguese. In this work, we document the development of ***GigaVerbo***, a concatenation of deduplicated
 Portuguese text corpora amounting to 200 billion tokens. Via this corpus, we trained a series of decoder-transformers
 named ***Tucano***. Our models perform equal or superior to other Portuguese and multilingual language models of similar size in several
 Portuguese benchmarks. The evaluation of our models also reveals that model performance on many currently available benchmarks
 used by the Portuguese NLP community has ***little to no correlation*** with the scaling of token ingestion during
 training, highlighting the limitations of such evaluations when it comes to the assessment of Portuguese generative language models.
 All derivatives of our study are openly released on GitHub and Hugging Face.

Our study brings the following advancements to the Portuguese NLP community:

1. The concatenation of a larger and more **high-quality dataset for Portuguese** language modeling ([**GigaVerbo**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo)).
2. The development of **learned filters and datasets** to improve text pre-processing for Portuguese.
3. Pushing self-supervised pretraining beyond the **500 billion tokens** mark for Portuguese monolingual models.
4. The development of new, low-resource, efficient, and effective **open-source language models for Portuguese** ([**Tucano**](https://huggingface.co/collections/TucanoBR/tucano-670565e8c5325fb7f2da4361)).
5. A critical assessment and comparison of currently available **benchmarks for Portuguese language models**.

## An Anthology of Portuguese LLM Development

Our study provides a historical overview of Portuguese LLM development from **2020 to October 2024**, allowing readers to better contextualize our and past works.

![This image illustrates several Portuguese language model releases from 2020 to June 2024.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/timeline.png)

## GigaVerbo

GigaVerbo contains over **145 million documents**, amounting to **780 GB of text**. Much like other text datasets, Gigaverbo was formed by concatenating several portions of openly available datasets for Portuguese and deduplicating their summation.

Our dataset is composed of the following subsets:

| **Subset** | **Nº of Samples** | **%** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **monoHPLT-PT** | 58,244,012 | 40.09% | The clean and deduplicated Portuguese portion of the High-Performance Language Technologies resources dataset. |
| **CrawlPT** | 43,846,974 | 30.17% | A deduplicated Portuguese corpus extracted from various web pages, concatenated from CC-100, Oscar, and BrWaC. |
| **Multilingual-C4** | 16,092,571 | 11.07% | The Brazilian Portuguese cleaned portion of the m-C4 dataset. |
| **Common Crawl** | 12,470,998 | 8.58% | A clean and deduplicated snapshot of the Common Crawl dataset (CC-MAIN-2023-23). |
| **BlogSet-BR** | 4,321,181 | 2.97% | A collection of blog posts written in Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **Instruct-PTBR** | 2,962,856 | 2.04% | A mix of multiple instruction datasets for various tasks, machine-translated from English to Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **Corpus Carolina** | 2,075,395 | 1.43% | An open corpus with varied typology in contemporary Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **UltrachatBR** | 1,255,091 | 0.86% | A Portuguese version (machine-translated) of the Ultrachat dataset. |
| **Wikipedia** | 1,101,475 | 0.76% | Cleaned Portuguese articles built from the Wikipedia dumps. |
| **CulturaX** | 999,994 | 0.69% | The Portuguese portion of CulturaX, a multilingual dataset with 167 languages. |
| **LegalPT** | 925,522 | 0.64% | A concatenation of publicly available legal data in Portuguese, including legislation, jurisprudence, and legal articles. |
| **Gpt4All** | 808,803 | 0.56% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of the Gpt4All dataset. |
| **Bactrian-X** | 66,994 | < 0.1% | The Portuguese portion of Bactrian-X, a collection of instruction-response pairs in 52 languages. |
| **XL-Sum** | 64,577 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of XL-Sum, a diverse dataset for abstractive summarization. |
| **Dolly 15K** | 28,401 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of Dolly 15K, an open-source dataset of instruction-following records generated by human annotators. |
| **CosmosQA** | 25,260 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of the CosmosQA dataset for commonsense-based reading comprehension. |
| **ROOTS** | 10,740 | < 0.1% | The Portuguese portion of the ROOTS corpus, a dataset spanning 59 languages. |

GigaVerbo is currently hosted on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo). More information can be found in its dataset card.

## GigaVerbo Text-Filter

With the help of **GPT-4o**, we scored over **100,000 samples of GigaVerbo in terms of their overall quality**. With these scored samples dataset, we trained classifiers to help us filter GigaVerbo from low-quality samples (our text-quality dataset is also available in [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo-Text-Filter)).

| **Class** | **Precision** | **Recall** | **F1-score** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **LaBSE + XGBoost** | Low | 0.89 | 0.81 | 0.85 |
| High | 0.92 | 0.96 | 0.94 |
| **BERTimbau** | Low | **0.99** | **0.97** | **0.98** |
| High | **0.99** | **0.99** | **0.99** |

The table above shows the evaluation scores for both our LaBSE + XGBoost and BERTimbau-based classifiers. All these models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR).

Like many other studies, we used a decoder-only Transformer based on the Llama architecture as the basis for our models. For convenience,
 we eventually refer to these models as Tucano *small*, *medium*, *large*, and *XL*,
 which respectively correspond to the **[160m](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-160m)**, **[630m](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-630m)**, **[1b1](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-1b1)**, and **[2b4](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-2b4)** models.

| **\(n_{param}\)** | **\(n_{layers}\)** | **\(d_{model}\)** | **\(d_{mlp}\)** | **\(n_{heads}\)** | **\(n_{KV-heads}\)** | **\(d_{head}\)** | **\(c_{length}\)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 162,417,408 | 12 | 768 | 3,072 | 12 | 12 | 64 | 2048 |
| 630,253,568 | 14 | 2,048 | 4,096 | 16 | 4 | 128 | 2048 |
| 1,100,048,384 | 22 | 2,048 | 5,632 | 32 | 4 | 64 | 2048 |
| 2,444,618,240 | 24 | 2,560 | 10,240 | 16 | 4 | 160 | 4096 |

Each model has a vocabulary size of 32,000. Tucano-160m, 630m, and 1b1 were trained with a context window of 2048 tokens, while the largest model (2b4) was trained with sequences of length 4096. All models uese the [TeenyTinyLlama](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/TeenyTinyLlama/) tokenizer.

![This image illustrates the training loss and perplexity of Tucano models.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/loss-perplexity.png)

All logs from our training runs recorded the loss, evaluation loss, the current value of the learning rate, and the gradient norm for that specific optimization step. These are all available on [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano).

## Benchmarks

During training, we saved several checkpoints for each model at intervals of approximately 10.5 billion tokens. For every checkpoint, we employed a comprehensive evaluation harness. This evaluation harness contains several Portuguese native evaluations and English benchmarks machine-translated into Portuguese.

| Benchmark | n-shot | Origin | Type | Metric |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ENEM | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| BLUEX | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| OAB Exams | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| ASSIN2 RTE | 15-shot | Native | Entailment | `f1 macro` |
| ASSIN2 STS | 10-shot | Native | Similarity | `pearson` |
| FAQUAD NLI | 15-shot | Native | Entailment | `f1 macro` |
| HateBR | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| PT Hate Speech | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| TweetSentBR | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| CALAME-PT | 0-shot | Native | Next Word Prediction | `acc` |
| ARC-Challenge | 25-shot | Translated | Q&A | `acc norm` |
| HellaSwag | 10-shot | Translated | Q&A | `acc norm` |
| TruthfulQA | 0-shot | Translated | Q&A | `bleurt` |
| LAMBADA | 0-shot | Translated | Next Word Prediction | `acc` |

To learn how to replicate our usage of this harness, please visit the evaluation section of our [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano/tree/main/evaluations/README.md) repository.

Our evaluations revealed that for several benchmarks, token ingestions (i.e., *how long a model is pre-trained on new tokens*) seem to **not be correlated to benchmark performance**. Hence, we hypothesize that results showing good performance on such benchmarks (i.e., above what a random guesser would achieve) might indicate not language modeling pretraining but overfitting to the style of evaluation these benchmarks bring.

For example, while certain benchmarks **show no change in performance, regardless of the number of tokens ingested**:

![Evaluation scores as a function of token ingestion for the BLUEX benchmark.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/evals-bluex.png)

Other benchmarks prove to be a **indicator of model improvement in terms of its language modeling capabilities** as pretraining progresses:

![Evaluation scores as a function of token ingestion for the CALAME-PT benchmark.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/evals-calame_pt.png)

## Results

Focusing only on the benchmarks that showed a significant correlation between language modeling pretraining and performance, we see that our largest models **outperformed several multilingual and natively pre-trained LLMs across nearly all benchmarks**, including the recently released Llama-3.2-1b. Our models also outperformed larger multilingual models, such as Bloom-1b7.

| **Average** | **Calame-PT** | **Lambada-PT** | **ARC-PT** | **HellaSwag-PT** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Llama-3.2-3B | 52 | 58.43 | 49.1 | 43.25 | 57.2 |
| **Tucano-2b4** | 43.58 | 59.06 | 37.67 | 30.43 | 47.17 |
| Llama-3.2-1B | 42.95 | 51.83 | 41.02 | 33.5 | 45.44 |
| **Tucano-1b1** | 41.55 | 58.24 | 34.7 | 30.43 | 42.84 |
| Gemma-2b | 40.38 | 51.16 | 39.88 | 37.95 | 32.53 |
| Bloom-1b7 | 40.37 | 55.64 | 31.98 | 30.34 | 43.52 |
| **Tucano-630m** | 39.5 | 56.55 | 33.13 | 28.89 | 39.41 |
| Gemma-2-2b | 39.21 | 56.7 | 47.1 | 24.19 | 28.85 |
| Bloom-1b1 | 38.18 | 52.94 | 30.22 | 29.83 | 39.74 |
| GlórIA-1b3 | 36.05 | 52.79 | 27.71 | 26.67 | 37.04 |
| **Tucano-160m** | 35.14 | 52.31 | 28.16 | 27.01 | 33.07 |
| Xglm-564m | 34.55 | 50.58 | 27.42 | 25.56 | 34.64 |
| Bloom-560m | 34.32 | 49.95 | 25.44 | 24.74 | 37.15 |
| TTL-460m | 33.78 | 49.42 | 23.29 | 29.4 | 33 |

| TTL-160m | 30.78 | 46.72 | 20.98 | 26.15 | 29.29 |
| Lola-v1 | 30.19 | 26.4 | 18.32 | 30.42 | 45.61 |
| GPorTuguese | 28.92 | 40.61 | 22.98 | 22.48 | 29.62 |

Meanwhile, our custom Portuguese evaluation, based on the [AlpacaEval](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/alpaca_eval) methodology, demonstrates that our instruct models, **[Tucano-1b1-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-1b1-Instruct)** and **[Tucano-2b4-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-2b4-Instruct)**,

All evaluations for all benchmarks that form our custom harness are available on our [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano/blob/main/evaluations/README.md) repository.

## How To Use

All our models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR), and can easily be used by any application in compliance with the **Apache 2.0 license**.

![Example code to use Tucano models.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/code-sample.png)

The Tucano series significantly contributes to the Portuguese NLP community in several ways. All **models, along with intermediary checkpoints, datasets, code implementations, and logs, are freely accessible through the repositories associated with this study**, setting the Tucano series apart from several other works.

In terms of open (and reproducible) development, many aspects of past studies are indeed closed. Given the level of computing needed to practice deep learning at such scales, a lack of reusable code and materials can seriously slow down the Portuguese NLP community's progress while hindering its sustainability. With **Tucano** and **GigaVerbo's** development, we hope to make this scenario more sustainable and open.

# Hugo Abonizio

---

### Hugo Abonizio has a total of 26 co-authors. Here are the top co-authors by number of shared publications:

---

#### Latest Publications

- ## [MonoByte: A Pool of Monolingual Byte-level Language Models](https://www.scilit.com/publications/33be1d55a33eb3a0a0200c6f3ba26237)
    by Hugo Abonizio, Leandro Rodrigues de Souza, Roberto Lotufo, Rodrigo Nogueira

    The zero-shot cross-lingual ability of models pretrained on multilingual and even monolingual corpora has spurred many hypotheses to explain this intriguing empirical result. However, due to the costs of pretraining, most research uses public models whose pretraining methodology, such as the choice of tokenization, corpus size, and computational budget, might differ drastically. When researchers pretrain their own models, they often do so under a constrained budget, and the resulting models might underperform significantly compared to SOTA models. These experimental differences led to various inconsistent conclusions about the nature of the cross-lingual ability of these models. To help further research on the topic, we released 10 monolingual byte-level models rigorously pretrained under the same configuration with a large compute budget (equivalent to 420 days on a V100) and corpora that are 4 times larger than the original BERT's. Because they are tokenizer-free, the problem of unseen token embeddings is eliminated, thus allowing researchers to try a wider range of cross-lingual experiments in languages with different scripts. Additionally, we release two models pretrained on non-natural language texts that can be used in sanity-check experiments. Experiments on QA and NLI tasks show that our monolingual models achieve competitive performance to the multilingual one, and hence can be served to strengthen our understanding of cross-lingual transferability in language models.

- ## [Toward Text Data Augmentation for Sentiment Analysis](https://www.scilit.com/publications/ef1e26d4eccc1f8eea9df3d7ee83fef6)
    by Hugo Queiroz Abonizio, Emerson Cabrera Paraiso, Sylvio Barbon

    A significant part of natural language processing (NLP) techniques for sentiment analysis is based on supervised methods, which are affected by the quality of data. Therefore, sentiment analysis needs to be prepared for data quality issues, such as imbalance and lack of labeled data. Data augmentation methods, widely adopted in image classification tasks, include data-space solutions to tackle the problem of limited data and enhance the size and quality of training datasets to provide better models. In this work, we study the advantages and drawbacks of text augmentation methods such as easy data augmentation, back-translation, BART, and pretrained data augmentor) with recent classification algorithms (long short-term memory, convolutional neural network, bidirectional encoder representations of transformers, support vector machine, gated recurrent units, random forests, and enhanced language representation with informative entities, that have attracted sentiment-analysis researchers and industry applications. We explored seven sentiment-analysis datasets to provide scenarios of imbalanced datasets and limited data to discuss the influence of a given classifier in overcoming these problems, and provide insights into promising combinations of transformation, paraphrasing, and generation methods of sentence augmentation. The results revealed improvements from the augmented dataset, mainly for reduced datasets. Furthermore, when balanced by augmenting the minority class, the datasets were found to have improved quality, leading to more robust classifiers. The contributions to this article include the taxonomy of NLP augmentation methods and their efficiency over several classifiers from recent research trends in sentiment analysis and related fields.

# The Game Awards 2023 Winners: The Full List

The Game Awards 2023 has ended, but not before it treated us to a celebration of the past and future of the world of gaming. While The Game Awards was filled with big reveals and news about upcoming games, it also obviously honored the incredible games and developers from the past year.

This article will gather all the big winners of the night, including the coveted Game of the Year award which, in [the behemoth that was 2023,](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=&ved=2ahUKEwix-fXchf-CAxU4kYkEHUKyD3sQFnoECBUQAQ&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ign.com%2Farticles%2Fbest-reviewed-games-of-2023&usg=AOvVaw1R1ie4c0IqKbK__v3J1rMZ&opi=89978449) is even more special. While this year was filled with games that all could have won Game of the Year in other years, only one could walk away with the award and this time it was Baldur's Gate 3.

Not only did Baldur's Gate 3 win Game of the Year and [shadow drop its Xbox version,](https://www.ign.com/articles/baldurs-gate-3-is-now-available-on-xbox-series-xs) but it also won Best Community Support, Best RPG, Best Multiplayer, and the Player's Voice category. Alan Wake 2 followed with 3 wins in the categories of Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, and Best Art Direction.

You can check out the full list of The Game Awards 2023 winners below, and also be sure to check out [our roundup of all the biggest reveals from The Game Awards!](https://www.ign.com/articles/the-game-awards-2023-everything-announced)

### **Game of the Year**

*Recognizing a game that delivers the absolute best experience across all creative and technical fields.*

- Alan Wake 2
- **Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- Resident Evil 4 Remake
- Super Mario Bros. Wonder
- The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

### **Best Game Direction**

*Awarded for outstanding creative vision and innovation in game direction and design.*

- **Alan Wake 2 - WINNER**
- Baldur's Gate 3
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- Super Mario Bros. Wonder
- The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

### **Best Narrative**

*For outstanding storytelling and narrative development in a game.*

- **Alan Wake 2 - WINNER**
- Baldur's Gate 3
- Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
- Final Fantasy 16
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2

### **Best Art Direction**

*For outstanding creative and/or technical achievement in artistic design and animation.*

- **Alan Wake 2 - WINNER**
- Hi-Fi Rush
- Lies of P
- Super Mario Bros. Wonder
- The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

### **Best Score/Music**

*For outstanding music, inclusive of score, original song and/or licensed soundtrack.*

- Alan Wake 2
- Baldur's Gate 3
- **Final Fantasy 16 - WINNER**
- Hi-Fi Rush
- The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

### **Best Audio Design**

*Recognizing the best in-game audio and sound design.*

- Alan Wake 2
- Dead Space Remake
- **Hi-Fi Rush - WINNER**
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- Resident Evil 4 Remake

### **Best Performance**

*Awarded to an individual for voice-over acting, motion and/or performance capture.*

- Ben Starr - Final Fantasy 16
- Cameron Monaghan - Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
- Idris Elba - Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
- Melanie Liburd - Alan Wake 2
- **Neil Newbon - Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Yuri Lowenthal - Marvel's Spider-Man 2

### **Games for Impact**

*For a thought-provoking game with a pro-social meaning or message.*

- A Space for the Unbound
- Chants of Sennaar
- Goodbye Volcano High
- **Tchia - WINNER**
- Terra Nil
- Venba

### **Best Ongoing Game**

*Awarded to a game for outstanding development of ongoing content that evolves the player experience over time.*

- Apex Legends
- **Cyberpunk 2077 - WINNER**
- Final Fantasy 14
- Fortnite
- Genshin Impact

### **Best Indie Game**

*For outstanding creative and technical achievement in a game made outside the traditional publisher system.*

- Cocoon
- Dave the Diver
- Dredge
- **Sea of Stars - WINNER**
- Viewfinder

### **Best Debut Indie Game**

*For the best debut game created by a new independent studio.*

- **Cocoon - WINNER**
- Dredge
- Pizza Tower
- Venba
- Viewfinder

### **Best Mobile Game**

*For the best game playable on a mobile device.*

- Final Fantasy 7: Ever Crisis
- **Honkai: Star Rail - WINNER**
- Hello Kitty Island Adventure
- Monster Hunter Now
- Terra Nil

### **Best Community Support**

*Recognizing a game for outstanding community support, transparency and responsiveness, inclusive of social media activity and game updates/patches.*

- **Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
- Destiny 2
- Final Fantasy 16
- No Man's Sky

### **Best VR/AR Game**

*For the best game experience playable in virtual or augmented reality, irrespective of platform.*

- Gran Turismo 7
- Humanity
- Horizon: Call of the Mountain
- **Resident Evil Village - WINNER**
- Synapse

### **Innovation in Accessibility**

*Recognizing software and/or hardware that is pushing the medium forward by adding features, technology and content to help games be played and enjoyed by an even wider audience.*

- Diablo 4
- **Forza Motorsport - WINNER**
- Hi-Fi Rush
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- Mortal Kombat 1
- Street Fighter 6

### **Best Action Game**

*For the best game in the action genre focused primarily on combat.*

- **Armored Core 6: Fires of Rubicon - WINNER**
- Dead Island 2
- Ghostrunner 2
- Hi-Fi Rush
- Remnant 2

### **Best Action/Adventure Game**

*For the best action/adventure game, combining combat with traversal and puzzle solving.*

- Alan Wake 2
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- Resident Evil 4
- Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
- **The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - WINNER**

### **Best RPG**

*For the best game designed with rich player character customization and progression, including massively multiplayer experiences.*

- **Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Final Fantasy 16
- Lies of P
- Sea of Stars
- Starfield

### **Best Fighting Game**

*For the best game designed primarily around head-to-head combat.*

- God of Rock
- Mortal Kombat 1
- Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2
- Pocket Bravery
- **Street Fighter 6 - WINNER**

### **Best Family Game**

*For the best game appropriate for family play, irrespective of genre or platform.*

- Disney Illusion Island
- Party Animals
- Pikmin 4
- Sonic Superstars
- **Super Mario Bros. Wonder - WINNER**

### **Best Sports/Racing Game**

*For the best traditional and non-traditional sports and racing game.*

- EA Sports FC 24
- F1 23
- **Forza Motorsport - WINNER**
- Hot Wheels Unleashed 2: Turbocharged
- The Crew Motofest

### **Best SIM/Strategy Game**

*Best game focused on real time or turn-based simulation or strategy gameplay, irrespective of platform.*

- Advanced Wars 1+" Re-Boot Camp
- Cities: Skylines 2
- Company of Heroes 3
- Fire Emblem Engage
- **Pikmin 4 - WINNER**

### **Best Multiplayer Game**

*For outstanding online multiplayer gameplay and design, including co-op and massively multiplayer experiences, irrespective of game genre or platform.*

- **Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Diablo 4
- Party Animals
- Street Fighter 6
- Super Mario Bros. Wonder

### **Content Creator of the Year**

*For a streamer or content creator who has made an important and positive impact on the community in 2021.*

- **IronMouse - WINNER**
- PeopleMakeGames
- Quackity
- Spreen
- SypherPK

### **Best Esports Athlete**

*The esports athlete judged to be the most outstanding for performance and conduct in 2021, irrespective of game.*

- **Lee “Faker” Sang-hyeok - WINNER**
- Mathieu “ZywOo” Herbaut
- Max “Demon1” Mazanov
- Paco “HyDra” Rusiewiez
- Park “Ruler” Jae-hyuk
- Phillip ”ImperialHal” Dosen

### **Best Esports Coach**

*The Esports coach judged to be the most outstanding for performance and conduct in 2021.*

- **Christine “potter” Chi - WINNER**
- Danny “zonic” Sorensen
- Jordan “Gunba” Graham
- Remy “XTQZZZ” Quoniam
- Yoon “Homme” Sung-young

### **Best Esports Event**

*Recognizing an event (across single or multiple days) that delivered a best-of-class experience for participants and the broadcast audience.*

- **2023 League of Legends World Championship - WINNER**
- Blast.tv Paris Major 2023
- EVO 2023
- The International Dota 2 Championships 2023
- VALORANT Champions 2023

### **Best Esports Game**

*For the game that has delivered the best overall esports experience to players (inclusive of tournaments, community support and content updates), irrespective of genre or platform.*

- Counter-Strike 2
- Dota 2
- Leage of Legends
- PUBG Mobile
- **Valorant - WINNER**

### **Best Esports Team**

*Recognizing a specific esports team (not the full organization) judged the most outstanding for performance and conduct in 2021.*

- Evil Geniuses
- Fnatic
- Gaimin Gladiators
- **JD Gaming - WINNER**
- Team Vitality

### **Most Anticipated Game**

*Recognizing an announced game that has demonstrably illustrated potential to push the gaming medium forward.*

- **Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth - WINNER**
- Hades 2
- Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth
- Star Wars Outlaws
- Tekken 8

### **Best Adaptation**

*Celebrating game-inspired projects across entertainment including TV, movies, comics, and more.*

- Castlevania: Nocturne
- Gran Turismo
- **The Last of Us - WINNER**
- The Super Mario Bros. Movie
- Twisted Metal

### **Players' Voice**

*This category is 100% voted on by fans for their favorite game of 2023.*

- **Baldur's Gate 3 - WINNER**
- Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
- Genshin Impact
- Marvel's Spider-Man 2
- The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

### The Game Awards 2023: Every Winner and Nominee

Baldur's Gate 3 won Game of the Year at the TGAs. The first 18 games on this list all won an award -- the rest were nominated and came up empty.

[See All](https://www.ign.com/playlist/igneditorial/lists/the-game-awards-2023-every-game-nominated "View All Games")

*Adam Bankhurst is a news writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter* [*@AdamBankhurst*](https://twitter.com/AdamBankhurst) *and on* [*Twitch.*](https://www.twitch.tv/AdamBankhurst)

# The Game Awards 2024 Winners: The Full List

## Here's all the nominees and a running list of winners from one of the biggest nights in gaming.

The Game Awards 2024 is in the books, and it brought a heap of [exciting news](https://www.ign.com/articles/the-game-awards-2024-everything-announced), including trailers for [The Witcher 4](https://www.ign.com/articles/inside-the-witcher-4-cd-projekt-reds-plans-for-its-next-big-rpg), [Okami 2](https://www.ign.com/articles/okami-2-unveiled-at-the-game-awards-2024), and [Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet](https://www.ign.com/articles/naughty-dog-heads-to-space-with-intergalactic-the-heretic-prophet-the-game-awards-2024), a new space adventure from Naughty Dog. Of course, in addition to giving us our first glimpse at what's coming in the world of gaming, the show also looked back, honoring the outstanding games – and developers who make them – of the last year.

Six games were nominated for the top prize of Game of the Year: [Astro Bot](https://www.ign.com/articles/astro-bot-review), [Balatro](https://www.ign.com/articles/balatro-review), [Black Myth: Wukong](https://www.ign.com/articles/black-myth-wukong-review-pc), [Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://www.ign.com/articles/final-fantasy-7-rebirth-review), [Metaphor: ReFantazio](https://www.ign.com/articles/metaphor-refantazio-review), and [Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree](https://www.ign.com/articles/elden-ring-shadow-of-the-erdtree-dlc-review), with Astro Bot taking home the top prize and three additional wins.
